researchQuestions.questionText: What does each box on a W-2 actually represent for a first-time filer, and why does Box 1 differ from gross salary?
How long does the IRS typically take to issue a refund after e-filing this season?
What does W-2 Box 12 code D mean for a typical salaried filer with an employer retirement plan?
Has the IRS refund processing timeline changed specifically for the current filing season compared to prior years?

evidence.claim: Box 1 reports federal taxable wages, which is lower than gross salary because it excludes certain pre-tax deductions.

evidenceText.text: Box 1 shows federal taxable wages, typically lower than gross salary because it excludes pre-tax deductions such as traditional 401(k) contributions and cafeteria plan benefits.

evidence.supportingContext: The IRS's own description of what each W-2 box represents, directly from the form's official guidance page.
evidence.notesForVerification: Confirm the specific list of pre-tax deduction types is current for the applicable tax year before treating it as exhaustive.

evidence.claim: The IRS states that most e-filed refunds with direct deposit are issued within 21 days.

evidenceText.text: most taxpayers who file electronically and choose direct deposit should expect their refund within 21 days of filing

evidence.supportingContext: Reuters reporting the IRS's own stated expectation at the opening of the filing season.
limitations: Reported by a news outlet rather than sourced directly from an IRS publication in the supplied materials.
evidence.notesForVerification: Cross-check against the IRS's own current-season refund guidance page for the exact wording and any caveats on covered credits.

evidence.claim: Some filers report refunds taking substantially longer than 21 days this season.

evidenceText.text: A filer reports still waiting eight weeks after filing, with other thread participants reporting similar delays.

evidence.supportingContext: Anecdotal community reports, not independently verified case details.
limitations: Anonymous, unverified anecdotal reports with no case-specific detail such as credits claimed.
Only a search snippet was seen; the full thread was never fetched.
evidence.notesForVerification: Determine whether reported delays correlate with returns claiming credits subject to mandatory review, which the IRS statement itself carves out as an exception.

evidence.claim: W-2 Box 12 code D generally denotes elective deferrals to a 401(k) cash or deferred arrangement.

evidenceText.text: Code D generally denotes elective deferrals to a 401(k) cash or deferred arrangement.

evidence.supportingContext: A payroll processor's general explainer on W-2 box codes.
limitations: No IRS or standards-body source in the supplied materials confirms this code definition directly.
evidence.notesForVerification: Confirm against the current IRS Form W-2 instructions' own Box 12 code table before treating this as authoritative.

conflicts.description: Reuters reporting cites an official IRS estimate of a 21-day refund turnaround, while a community forum discussion reports refunds taking eight weeks or more this season.
conflicts.possibleReason: The delayed cases may involve credits subject to mandatory review, which the IRS statement itself notes can extend the typical timeline; alternatively the forum reports may be unrepresentative or unverified.

gaps.description: No supplied material specifically addresses whether IRS refund processing timelines changed for the current filing season versus prior seasons; available materials describe the current season's stated timeline only, not a year-over-year comparison.
Box 12 code D guidance is only supported by a company blog search snippet; no IRS or standards-body primary source was found in the supplied materials.
